findings.text: The 32-bit compatibility MTRR descriptors use compact compatibility integer fields. The set form carries base plus size and type. The get form adds a register number ahead of the same three fields. Both describe one variable range by location, extent and memory type.

The 32-bit MTRR control family uses ioctl base M with operation numbers zero through nine. Number zero adds, one sets, two deletes, three gets, four kills, five adds a page entry, six sets a page entry, seven deletes a page entry, eight gets a page entry and nine kills a page entry. Get operations transfer in both directions while the others transfer toward the kernel, with the set structure used for all but get and the get structure used for get.
MTRR state reporting shifts the default-type enable flags down by ten positions to form compact state bits for fixed-range enable and overall enable.

Monitor-wait hint handling treats the hint as two four-bit fields with width four. Both substate and C-state masks equal fifteen, with C-state extracted by shifting then masking and substate by masking. The C1 substate mask equals 240. CPUID leaf five ECX uses bit zero for extension support and bit one for interrupt break. Monitor-wait ECX uses bit zero for interrupt break, AMD extended wait uses bit one for timer enable with an all-ones cycle limit and disable pattern 240. Timed pause uses encodings one and zero.

Low-level idle primitives wrap single instructions with register-passed operands. Monitor and extended monitor arm address monitoring with pointer plus two control words. Wait and extended wait enter the hinted state with hint plus control words, extended wait adding a cycle budget. A combined enable-interrupt plus wait form exists, as does a timed-pause form taking three control words.

Idle with hints follows a polling-aware sequence. It exits immediately when scheduling is pending, clears CPU buffers, and stays in polling mode when polling is already active unless a monitor erratum forces the monitor path. Otherwise it monitors the current thread flag word, rechecks for pending schedule, then waits with interrupts either left controlled by the hint break flag or enabled across wait with restoration afterward, finally clearing polling state.

Nonmaskable-interrupt handling distinguishes local, unknown, serial-error and IO-check sources with a count terminator. Handlers return done as zero or handled as one and receive a type plus register snapshot. Each registration links into a list and records handler address, maximum duration, flags and name. A first flag with value one requests head insertion.

The NMI registration helper creates a static action object named from the handler, initializes its list linkage, handler, name and flags, then forwards type and object to the core registration routine.
One NOP family defines approved padding lengths one through eight with maximum eight, where longer forms build on shorter ones with prefixes or displacements.
A second NOP family defines padding lengths one through eleven with maximum eleven, adding distinct encodings for nine, ten and eleven built by prefixing shorter forms.
Assembly string macros expose the one-through-eight byte NOP sequences for inline use, with additional string forms for nine through eleven in the second family.

Return-depth tracking uses a five-bit shift quantum with sixteen stuffing iterations. Normal reset starts from the top bit set, call-entry reset starts from top byte 252, and credit uses all bits set.
Call-thunk debug counting has two configurations. One increments per-CPU call, return, stuff and context-switch counters. The other defines all four increments as empty.

Call-depth maintenance also has active and empty configurations. The active form can credit depth to minus one, reset to initial patterns for normal and call entry, and increment by arithmetic shifting the per-CPU depth while counting calls. The empty form defines all four operations as no-ops.
Retpoline thunks occupy thirty-two bytes and return-stack-buffer clearing iterates thirty-two times to overwrite all entries.

Return-buffer filling builds on a single slot that performs an annotated intra-function call followed by a trap. One buffer strategy loops over slot pairs with stack adjustment, misprediction fence, depth credit and context-switch counting. The other unrolls slots by count with a single stack adjustment. A single-return helper emits one slot plus adjustment and fence.

Interrupted safereturn handling checks whether the saved instruction pointer lies within a five-byte window starting at a named return site. Only in-window cases serialize and delegate to a handler with the register frame; otherwise execution falls through.

Return-untraining selects reset behavior by feature: entry barrier with normal reset, exit barrier with normal reset for virtual machines, and entry barrier with call-entry reset. Unret-safe annotation aliases retpoline-safe. CPU-buffer clearing issues a supervisor selector verify-write, exposed as a stringified form and gated by an alternative that is empty without the clear-buffers feature.

APIC-to-node mapping either stores into a table or does nothing when NUMA is disabled, in which case CPU-to-node always reports no node. A separate disabled configuration defines node set, clear, CPU init, add, remove and giant-node init as empty and reports one physical node.

Numachip control registers encode node number by shifting sixteen bits with a twelve-bit node mask allowing four thousand nodes, and mask offsets to low fifteen bits. Node-ID group offset is eight and external-interrupt-generation group offset combines 48 with group three shifted twelve.

First-generation local control mapping spans a fixed high window from base 0x3FFFFE000000 to limit 0x3FFFFFFFFFFF with derived size and eight LAPIC bits. Address construction combines the window base with bit fifteen set, a broadcast node pattern and the masked offset, then reads and writes with byte swapping around word access.

Second-generation mapping uses base 0xF0000000 with one-megabyte size and dedicated offsets 0x100000 for interrupt command, 0x200000 for timer deadline, 0x200008 for timer interrupt, 0x200018 for current time and 0x200020 for reset. Addresses mask the offset into the window. Word and double-word accessors pass through directly, and a timer selector derives an index from CPU number modulo forty-eight shifted by six.
OLPC platform state records flag bits plus a board revision. Presence flag equals one and display-controller flag equals two.

Board identity helpers encode an identifier by shifting left four, adding eight for final builds and zero for pre builds. Revision comparison checks at-least against stored revision. Presence and display-controller queries test flag bits when enabled and report false when disabled.

OLPC GPIO assignments fix microphone to one, display status zero to five, status one to six, interrupt to seven, thermal alarm to Geode ten, load to eleven, blank to twelve, SMBus clock to fourteen, data to fifteen, auxiliary to Geode twenty-four, lid to twenty-six and embedded-controller interrupt to twenty-seven.
OLPC firmware interface reserves page-directory entry one thousand twenty-two and uses signature 0x2057464F.
The firmware call wrapper passes name plus array sizes and pointers to a core routine. Detection, page-table setup and device-tree build are empty when the interface is disabled.
ORC metadata places a hash header in a dedicated aligned section. Lookup divides the kernel text range between start and end symbols into two-hundred-fifty-six-byte blocks ordered by eight.

ORC register codes assign zero to undefined, one to AX, two to DX, three to SP, four to BP, five to DI, six to R10, seven to R13, eight to previous SP, nine to indirect SP, ten to indirect BP and fifteen as maximum. Entry types assign zero to undefined, one to end of stack, two to call, three to registers and four to partial registers.

Each ORC entry stores signed stack and base offsets plus compact fields for stack register, base register, type and signal, with field order swapped by endianness and overall packing to avoid padding.
User-page copying ignores address and page context and delegates to page copying, which on 32-bit moves a full page via memory copy.

The 64-bit page-copy entry provides a typed function that moves a page with an optimized string operation, using an alternative to select a register-based fallback when the fast repeat feature is unavailable.

Boot address helpers alias the normal virtual-physical conversions. Canonical-address helpers sign-extend through shift round-trip and test equality. A zeroed movable folio allocator combines high-user movable zeroed flags with order zero. Huge-TLB unmapped-area support is declared present.

32-bit physical conversion subtracts the page offset with symbol conversion identical and relocation hiding as identity against zero. Page offset and kernel map share the configured base. Thread size doubles one page, IRQ stack matches thread size, and one exception stack is reserved.

Address mask widths have a wide physical configuration of fifty-two and a narrow physical configuration of thirty-two while virtual width stays thirty-two. User task size, low and max sizes, default mapping window and stack tops all equal the page offset with IA32 offset identical. Kernel image allowance is five hundred twelve megabytes.

Entering monitor-wait while scheduling is pending or without clearing polling state risks missed wakeups. The idle sequence therefore rechecks scheduling after arming and always clears polling, and pairs interrupt enable across wait with restoration.

NMI handlers record a maximum duration, implying overrun hazards if handlers exceed their budget. Return-stack filling must fully overwrite entries and serialize to avoid mispredicted returns; incomplete stuffing or missing fences leave speculative hazards.

Local control mapping also relies on an external address conversion from the startup source.

32-bit page copy also relies on external memory copy from boot copy support.
32-bit page copy also relies on external memory copy from boot string header.

Idle entry relies on external polling-set-and-test, second variant.
